ticket.title: Split reconciliation out of migrate: cleanup must not ride on a path that only runs when legacy work exists
acceptance_criteria: DONE 2026-11-06. Root cause of the silent no-op
found by instrumenting rather than guessing: toml::Value's FromStr parses a TOML *value*
not a document
so the file's opening '[storypole]' was read as an array and the parser then hit 'unexpected content
expected nothing' at the closing bracket. The config was always valid; the parser was being asked the wrong question. Fixed by using toml::from_str
which parses a document.\n\nSecond correctness fix: comparing tables for exact equality was too strict. The per-tool file is a stale SUBSET (same prefix
same TTL
but verification_commands = [] against unified's real chain)
so equality would have left the duplicate forever. A file is now redundant when every key it holds exists upstream with the same value
and informative the moment one key differs or is absent upstream - which is what it then reports

naming the key.\n\nResolution executed: tidy flagged all ten with the precise conflict ('would lose verification_commands (differs from the unified value)'); each was verified by script to hold no information the unified file lacks
then removed with its own commit. tidy now reports 'Nothing to reconcile' in every repo
and zero per-tool configs remain.\n\nNote on the rule NOT baked in: the tool does not treat empty-vs-populated as auto-resolvable. That judgement is explicit in the commit message instead
because [] in a stale copy means absence while [] in a live file can mean intent.
